why: The record 'deceived' also rests on Job 12:16, where the Hebrew is shagag (err, go astray), a different word from the Greek planomenoi of Titus 3:3 that deceived_assessment rests on. Merging would fold a Job sense into the Titus state; the shared Titus 3:3 state can be linked instead.

Gen 35:19 identifies the two in the text itself: 'on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem)', with the Hebrew hi' (that is) between the names; Mic 5:2 calls it Bethlehem Ephrathah. beth_lehem already lists Ephrath as an alias, and Gen 35:16 is the same place on the road.

Both are Judah's Canaanite wife, the daughter of Shua (Gen 38:2, Gen 38:12). 1Chr 2:3 names her Bath-shua as the mother of Er, Onan and Shelah, the three sons Gen 38:3-5 gives her, and judahs_wife already carries that reference.

Job 11:14 'tents' is one occurrence of the object tent (Hebrew ohel), and tent is a pattern record spanning seven verses from Gen 9:21 to Job 18:6. An instance stays apart from the pattern it belongs to; the Job 11:14 link should be an instance link, not a second record.

Same name, same Berean heading and the same four passages (Matt 26:31-35; Mark 14:27-31; Luke 22:31-38; John 13:36-38), and the relations point to the same tellings. The trailing underscore marks a duplicate.

Both have the same name and start at Num 11:1, but one telling runs to 11:35 and the other to 11:9, and the graph already records the shorter as lying within the longer. A different extent is a different occurrence, so these stay apart; if Doug judges them one episode, the longer span is the one to keep.

Same name, both starting at Num 13:1, but one telling ends at 13:33 (the sending and the report) and the other runs to 14:45 (the people's refusal and the rout at Hormah, Num 14:45). Containment is recorded, so these are a shorter and a longer span, not one occurrence; if Doug judges them one event, keep the longer span.
Both are Job's unnamed wife at Job 2:9, who says 'Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die.' The same woman at the same verse; jobs_wife carries that speech and seven relations.
Both record the one assessment at Titus 3:7, being justified by his grace (Greek dikaiothentes te ekeinou chariti). The wording differs only by 'his'; justified_by_grace has the wider relations.
Both are Elon the Hittite, father of Basemath, at Gen 26:34. The disambiguation of elon names the same man; elon also carries Gen 36:2 (Adah), so it has the wider record.

Gen 23:17 deeds two things to Abraham: 'the field ... at Machpelah' and 'the cave that was in it', so the text separates the cave from the property. machpelah describes the field with its cave, while cave_of_machpelah is the cave; the located_in relations already state the containment.

Gen 2:8 'a garden in Eden' and Gen 2:15 and 3:23-24 'the Garden of Eden' name one garden, the same Hebrew gan in both records. garden has only Gen 2:8, which eden already carries; eden keeps Ezek 28:13 and the wider relations.

Gen 13:18 'the oaks of Mamre' is the site named Mamre, and Gen 18:1 uses the same oaks-of-Mamre phrase for the place where the visitors came, which mamre_site describes. Medium because one record names the spot by its oaks (elonei) and the other by Mamre, two words for one site.

Job 1:18-19 is one messenger's report, the fourth of the four in the chapter ('another messenger came' at 1:18, then 'suddenly a mighty wind' at 1:19). job_1_19_messenger is only the 1:19 part of that same speech.
Mark 1:23 and Luke 4:33 are two gospel accounts of one man in the Capernaum synagogue who cries out with an unclean spirit. The keep has five relations; its refs should gain Luke 4:33 on merge.

Mark 2:3 and Luke 5:18 are one paralytic brought by four men to Jesus at Capernaum, and sick_of_the_palsy carries the Mark 2:12 healing relations. Its id is KJV wording ('sick of the palsy'), so the merged name must be the BSB 'the paralytic'.

Both are the one formula at Titus 3:8, the saying that is trustworthy (BSB 'This saying is trustworthy'). The keep has three relations including Paul as speaker. Its desc and the other record's desc use KJV wording ('This is a faithful saying'), so the merged desc must be rewritten in BSB.
Both give the one verdict at Titus 3:2, 'to malign no one' (Greek medena blasphemein), in the same words. speaking_evil_of_no_man has no relations; the keep has two.
Both are Paul's command at Titus 3:2 'to malign no one' (blasphemein), with the same verse and the same desc. The keep has seven relations.

2Kgs 23:36 and 2Chr 36:5 tell the same reign in the same words (the Hebrew of both: 'twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem'), as parallel tellings, as the four Gospel tellings are one event. Medium because the books differ in detail (Kings gives the mother Zebidah; Chronicles adds the captivity at 2Chr 36:6), which is not a conflict on any fact both state.

Both are the one phrase at Titus 3:8, 'excellent and profitable for the people' (Greek kala kai ophelima tois anthropois), same verse, one relation each. Both descs use KJV wording ('unto men'), so the merged desc must be BSB.
Both record Paul's one instruction at Titus 3:12 to come to him at Nicopolis, with the same sentence in both descs. The keep has five relations.

Both rest on the one Titus 3:2 prohibition, 'to malign no one' (blasphemein), and not_speaking_evil is that prohibition phrased as a state. Neither record has relations, so the merge should take the relations of the obligation record (see pair 17). Medium because state and prohibition differ in mood.

Both are the verdict at Titus 3:1 to obey the magistrates, the Greek peitharchein (to be obedient). obey_magistrates_obligation has two relations and the other none. Medium because 'obedient to' is a state while 'obligation to obey' is a duty.
Both are the one instruction at Titus 3:1 to be subject to rulers and authorities and ready for every good work, with the same desc. The keep has eight relations.

Both are the one statement at Titus 3:4, 'the kindness of God our Savior and His love for mankind appeared' (Greek epephanē), with the same words. titus_3_4_claim has five relations. Pairs 25-27 are one statement recorded three times and should collapse to one record.
Same statement at Titus 3:4 with the same words; titus_3_4_statement has five relations. Part of the three-record group with pairs 25 and 27.

Same statement at Titus 3:4 in the same words, and both records have five relations, so the keep is the claim record by the naming the other pairs use. Part of the three-record group with pairs 25 and 26.

2Kgs 12:21 names the conspirator Jozabad son of Shimeath, in Hebrew Yozabad, and 2Chr 24:26 names him Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite, in Hebrew Zabad, so the rule keeps them apart. They are probably one man (same father, same killing of Joash), but the text gives two names and gives Jehozabad two different fathers across the books (Shomer in Kings, Shimrith in Chronicles), a tension the text holds; Doug may decide to link them as a probable identity.

Both rest on the one Titus 3:2 prohibition, 'to malign no one' (blasphemein); not_speaking_evil's desc 'the absence of evil speech' is the same prohibition as a state. Medium for the same reason as pair 22: state against duty.

Both have the same two refs (Gen 1:26 and 1:28) and the same speaks_of relation, 'over the fish of the sea' (Hebrew dagat hayyam in both verses). Same words at the same verses; the keep carries the text's phrase.

Both give the one directive at Titus 3:10, 'Reject a divisive man after a first and second admonition' (Greek hairetikon anthropon ... paraitou). One record names the act and the other the rule, so medium; the keep has two relations, including the admonition. The id rejecting_heretick uses KJV wording ('heretick').
